subject: SLA exemption request: filtering/tool-call & structured-output incidents — proposed short-term plan
messages:
From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@blueharbor.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Connors <tim.connors@blueharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: production impact — filtering + tool-calls failing during peak window

Hi Mina,

Quick summary from our side: over the morning peak (2026-09-15 08:05–08:42 PDT) we saw ~18% of requests return a tool-call error or malformed structured output after Redwood's content filter conversion. The errors caused our downstream orchestration to retry and drop ~6% of patient-facing notifications (alerts were delayed or suppressed).

We pulled logs and attached a compressed support_log_20260915.txt with examples. The failures appear correlated to a filter-evaluation timeout and a subsequent tool-invocation exception (timeout 502 / structured schema mismatch).

Because we operate in a regulated environment, uptime and timely delivery are contractual. We need Redwood to confirm whether these filter/tool-call failure classes can be considered an SLA exclusion while you deploy mitigations. If not, please propose the compensatory credits and a clear mitigation timeline.

Requested from Redwood:
- A short-term exemption or formal SLA addendum for filter-triggered tool-call / structured-output failures for up to 30 days while fixes roll out.
- A technical summary of cause and planned mitigations (root cause + ETA).
- A DocuSign link or draft addendum we can circulate to our procurement/legal team.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Zhou
Head of Integrations, BlueHarbor Health
claire.zhou@blueharbor.com

Attachment: support_log_20260915.txt (sample error traces)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production impact — filtering + tool-calls failing during peak window

Claire — thanks for the clear write-up and the logs. We’re prioritizing this. High-level response while we investigate deeper:

1) Short-term: we can provision a controlled SLA addendum that excludes stated failure classes (content-filter evaluation timeouts and downstream tool-invocation exceptions that originate from filter-induced payload changes) for an initial 30-day window. We will provide a formal addendum and a DocuSign link within 48 hours.

2) Near-term mitigation plan (owner: Aditya): revert affected routes to a conservative filter-mode (fail-open fallback) during peak windows and enable a model-level structured-output validator to prevent schema-level rejections. This should reduce retries and missed notifications immediately.

3) Longer-term: kernel/queue-level improvements and more robust graceful-degradation for tool-calls are targeted in the upcoming infra release (ETA 3 weeks). Marcus will coordinate rollout and can provide pre-production test results to your team.

I’ve attached a draft addendum (draft-sla-addendum.pdf) and a service snapshot with the traces we’ve pulled. Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to align on exact language and the MSP/Procurement path? Proposed times: 10:00 or 14:00 PDT.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability 
Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: draft-sla-addendum.pdf, service_snapshot_20260916.json

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production impact — filtering + tool-calls failing during peak window

Claire and team — digging into the traces (see service snapshot), here are the technical observations and the concrete proposal for the addendum language: 

Observations:
- The majority of failures stem from an internal filter-evaluation path that, under high concurrency, hits a synchronous external rule-check and returns an altered payload that causes downstream tool-call deserialization to fail (schema mismatch) or the tool call to time out.
- Errors are predominantly transient (95th percentile resolved on retry within 8s), but retries trigger orchestrator backpressure and cause dropouts.

Immediate mitigations (we will enact these in the next 6–12 hours):
- Enable filter fail-open at the route-level for high-throughput endpoints during your configured peak window.
- Deploy a structured-output pre-flight validator that rejects invalid schemas before tool invocation and falls back to a baseline generation mode (without tool-calling).

Proposed SLA addendum excerpt (for legal):
- "SLA Exclusion: For a period of thirty (30) days following execution of this Addendum, failures attributable to Redwood's content filtering evaluation (including but not limited to filter-evaluation timeouts) or resulting downstream tool-invocation errors (including structured-output schema mismatches) will be excluded from SLA uptime/latency calculations for affected routes, provided Redwood implements the agreed mitigations and communicates scheduled changes to Customer. Credits for incidents not covered by this exclusion shall be governed by Section X of the Agreement."

Please let us know if BlueHarbor requires tighter language (specific error codes, time windows). We will prepare the DocuSign envelope as Mina suggested.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: production impact — filtering + tool-calls failing during peak window

Mina / Aditya — thank you. The proposed exemption language looks workable from our procurement side; legal asked for one tweak to be explicit about error codes and a 30-day review checkpoint.

We can sign the addendum with the tweak: add a clause that the exclusion applies only to documented filter-evaluation timeouts and tool-invocation exceptions with the listed error codes (502, 504, FILTER_TIMEOUT) and that both parties will reconvene at day 21 to review metrics and extend/terminate the exemption.

Please send the DocuSign link and we’ll loop in procurement. We also accept the proposed mitigations — Tim will run a quick integration smoke test after you enable the fail-open mode.

Claire
Claire Zhou
Head of Integrations, BlueHarbor Health
